Americans spend billions of hours on taxes—and even more time arguing about them based on myths. The top 1% already pay 40% of income taxes, corporations pass their tax burden to workers, and no tax on the rich can fix a deficit driven by entitlement spending, argues @veroderugy.
ow.ly/U0CE50YSZT3

Proclaiming Liberty is a fast-paced intellectual history that traces how John Adams, Thomas Jefferson, and their contemporaries transformed centuries of political thought into the revolutionary principles of the Declaration of Independence—and why those principles still matter today. 
 
Available May 5, 2026. Pre-order now!  
ow.ly/Z6EW50YR6OG

“The federal indictment against James Comey has ventured into the realm of legal parody,” writes Cato’s @foxmike90. He explains that this case exposes a more systemic pathology: the total lack of accountability for prosecutors. 

ow.ly/7UhO50YSZz3

The FCC's unprecedented review of ABC-Disney’s broadcast licenses shows the need to protect free expression, says Cato’s @dr_inserra. 
  
“It is past time for Congress to strip the FCC of its censorial powers,” he writes. 
  
ow.ly/wHwB50YSZsh

Even if Section 702 lapses for a bit, the US will still be able to identify and stop terrorists overseas plotting to attack America, says Cato’s @PGEddington.  
 
“What’s most important is getting a final FISA Section 702 reform that ensures the FBI needs probable cause to rummage through American’s digital data swept up under this program.” 
ow.ly/H5KY50YSZmg

The Iran war is reaching the 60-day mark. The War Powers Resolution isn't a blank check for open-ended war. In a new Cato Podcast episode, Molly Nixon and @katherinet57 examine what the law actually says, and how President Trump's use of military force in Iran tests its limits. 
  
Listen on Apple, Spotify, and our website!
Apple: ow.ly/kn0x50YSQ9e
Spotify: ow.ly/AxOJ50YSQ9k
Our website: ow.ly/iQWO50YSQ9h

Kansas is right to question coercive DEI mandates—but anti-DEI laws have their own risk: politicians deciding what counts as “legitimate knowledge.” Cato’s @Rhetors_of_York argues these bans can chill teaching on race, civil rights, and related ideas even without banning courses outright. 

Read more: ow.ly/9xyz50YS4ub

Two cabinet posts have acting leaders with unclear term limits. Cato’s Thomas A. Berry explains how some statutes bypass federal time limits—and why it matters. 
ow.ly/YBQ550YRYjP

“Being rooted in principle, being seen as having a high level of integrity and credibility, is a very important element in having influence, exerting influence, and ultimately persuading people.” — Peter Goettler.   
 
President and CEO of the Cato Institute joined the Chief Influencer podcast to discuss how principled leadership can be a powerful force for influence in Washington and beyond.  
 
Watch or listen the full conversation here:   
YouTube: ow.ly/Kv7y50YSvrT  
Amazon Music: ow.ly/BCu8

Congress should abolish the Renewable Fuel Standard, not tinker with it. Expanding E15 gasoline and changing the small refiner exemption without repealing ethanol subsidies is a giveaway to Big Ag and large refiners. Let ethanol compete on its own merits, argues Cato’s Travis Fisher. 

ow.ly/rqlT50YRYcm

Housing is the largest single expense for most Americans and has been at the frontline of “affordability” politics.  

At the Cato Institute, we developed federal, state, and local policy ideas to improve housing affordability. 

Check out our “Handbook on Affordability”: ow.ly/j9J250YR43q

Smarter defense spending beats bigger budgets. Cato’s Benjamin Giltner argues we should cut wasteful programs to make the Pentagon more efficient.
ow.ly/6utt50YRSui

Blaming social media for teen mental health is politically convenient. But it distracts from the data showing that teen mental health is tied to a variety of deeper issues and offline pressures, explains Cato's @jrhuddles:  
ow.ly/3Im150YRYeF

Whether through deliberate restraint or fiscal pressure, the US commitment to European security is likely to shrink by 2035. European NATO members shouldn’t wait to find out by how much. They should be able to defend themselves without Washington, argue Cato’s @JustinTLogan and Rachel Tausendfreund.

ow.ly/ryK450YR3Nu
Cato's “Handbook on Affordability” offers over 100 policy ideas that actually address the root causes, not just the symptoms: cato.org/affordability

Washington's policies aren't solving the affordability crisis — they're fueling it. Here's what would actually work.

Video

AI will undoubtedly disrupt more jobs over time, but comparative advantage doesn’t disappear because AI gets better: when machines do more of certain tasks, humans will shift toward other jobs, and whole new industries will emerge.
Anthropic’s early labor-market evidence finds no increase in unemployment in the most AI-exposed occupations, but slower hiring for younger workers, while overall US unemployment remains at 4.3%.
